questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Iraq?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Iraq article.

questions.proof: The capital of Iraq is Baghdad.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Iraq?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Iraq on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Iraq article.

questions.proof: Iraq borders Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to the south, Turkey to the north, Syria to the northwest, Jordan to the west, and Iran to the east.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The country was initially split into three zones: the American occupation zone, the British occupation zone, and the Polish occupation zone, similar to the way _____ was divided after World War II.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “divided”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Iraq article, under the heading “Politics”.

questions.proof: The country was initially split into three zones: the American occupation zone, the British occupation zone, and the Polish occupation zone, similar to the way Germany was divided after World War II.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Forces from _____ controlled areas in the British occupation zone.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “controlled”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Iraq article, under the heading “Politics”.
